answer: A farm cannot fake the aggregate without controlling every key it names, and hence paying the bridge bond on all of them and exposing each to the vine slash. Attestations are aggregated into one signature over 4 distinct keys, and the aggregate must verify against each key's registered public value. Because the sonnet audit verifies the aggregate, a single forged member invalidates the whole batch. Each impostor pays 15 dollars up front. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
